about.title: About WinsAlt
about.what: A WINS replacement: NetBIOS name server (RFC 1001/1002) with replication between WinsAlt servers and a web dashboard.
about.license: Released under the MIT License. It comes with no warranty of any kind.
about.files: The full license texts are in LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md in the installation folder.
setting.Wins:ListenAddress.label: Listen address
setting.Wins:ListenAddress.help: The IP address of this machine on which the name server receives packets (UDP).
- The IP of one adapter: serve and publish this machine's name on that network only (useful on a machine with several adapters)
Nothing else may hold UDP 137 on the address used:
- Windows: switch off NetBIOS over TCP/IP on that adapter (table on the Overview page)
- Linux: stop Samba's nmbd (systemctl disable --now nmbd)
setting.Wins:Port.label: UDP port
setting.Wins:Port.help: The port that receives name queries and registrations.
Every client always uses port 137 and cannot be told otherwise, so this should stay 137.
setting.Wins:AnswerBroadcasts.label: Answer broadcast queries
setting.Wins:AnswerBroadcasts.help: A WINS server normally answers only packets sent to it directly (unicast).
- ON: also answer broadcast queries, for devices on the same network that have no WINS server set
- OFF: ignore every broadcast (classic WINS behaviour)
When on, only names that are found get an answer. There is no "not found" answer, and no registration is accepted from a broadcast.
setting.Wins:QueueCapacity.label: Packet queue size
setting.Wins:QueueCapacity.help: How many packets can wait to be processed, per worker.
When the queue is full, new packets are dropped (counted under "Dropped" on the Overview page).
Raise it only if you see Dropped growing.
setting.Wins:QueryLogCapacity.label: Query log size
setting.Wins:QueryLogCapacity.help: How many recent entries the Query log tab keeps.
Kept in memory only, and gone when the service restarts.
setting.Wins:ConflictPolicy.label: Name conflict policy
setting.Wins:ConflictPolicy.help: What happens when a machine asks to register a unique name that another IP already holds.
- Challenge (as WINS does): ask the current owner first
If the owner still answers, the newcomer is refused
If it stays silent, the name goes to the newcomer (for example a machine that got a new IP from DHCP)
- Overwrite: the latest request always gets the name, nobody is asked
- Reject: the current owner always wins until the name expires or is released
setting.Wins:MinTtlSeconds.label: Minimum registration lifetime
setting.Wins:MinTtlSeconds.help: The shortest lifetime of a registered name.
A client that asks for less gets this value.
- Must not be longer than the maximum registration lifetime
Applies to the next registration or refresh.
Names already registered keep their lifetime until they are refreshed.
setting.Wins:MaxTtlSeconds.label: Maximum registration lifetime
setting.Wins:MaxTtlSeconds.help: The longest lifetime of a registered name, also used when a client does not ask for one.
Clients refresh by themselves after about half of it.
Shorter: names of machines that were switched off disappear sooner, at the cost of more refresh packets.
Keep the same minimum and maximum on every WinsAlt server that replicates with this one.
setting.Wins:SweepIntervalSeconds.label: Expiry sweep interval
setting.Wins:SweepIntervalSeconds.help: How often expired names are removed from the database.
An expired name is not answered from the moment it expires anyway.
This round only frees memory and records an event.
setting.Wins:PersistIntervalSeconds.help: How often the database is saved to wins-db.json.
It is saved only when something changed, and once more when the service stops.
After a sudden power loss, names registered since the last save are missing until their clients refresh.
setting.Wins:RegisterSelf.label: Publish this server's own name
setting.Wins:RegisterSelf.help: Once the operating system's own NetBIOS is off so that the service can use UDP 137, nothing else announces this machine's name.
- OFF: nothing is announced. Use this when nobody should find this machine by its NetBIOS name
setting.Wins:SelfName.label: Name to publish
setting.Wins:SelfName.help: The NetBIOS name published for this machine.
A host name still set to "localhost" is not published: set a real one, or a name here.
setting.Wins:SelfSuffixes.label: Suffixes to publish
setting.Wins:SelfSuffixes.help: The roles (2-digit hex suffixes) the machine name is published with, separated by commas.
1B, 1C and 1D are not accepted: they are the domain master browser, domain controller and master browser roles, which this service does not perform.
If the machine really is a domain controller, add it as a static mapping instead.
setting.Wins:SelfGroup.label: Workgroup / domain
setting.Wins:SelfGroup.help: The workgroup or domain this machine is registered as a member of.
- Empty: detect it (Windows: the machine's workgroup or domain; Linux: workgroup in /etc/samba/smb.conf when Samba is installed)
- "-" (a dash): not a member of any group
setting.Wins:Security:RegistrationMode.h: - Dynamic: any machine whose packets reach this server (classic WINS)
- AllowedSubnets: only machines in the networks listed in Allowed subnets
Machines outside the list cannot register, refresh or release, but can still query
- StaticOnly: no registration at all; only static mappings and replicated names are answered
Careful: a restricted mode lets the names of machines outside it expire and disappear.
setting.Wins:Security:AllowedSubnets.hel: The networks allowed to register in AllowedSubnets mode, in CIDR form, separated by commas.
List every network that has clients before switching the mode.
The addresses in use are on the Registered names tab.
setting.Wins:Security:RequireAddressMatc: - ON: refuse a registration or release whose IP differs from the packet's source IP
Stops one machine from registering a name for another machine's IP
Careful: a machine with several adapters (for example LAN + Wi-Fi) registers the IPs of all of them through one adapter, so part of it is refused.
setting.Wins:Security:BlockedNames.label: Blocked names
setting.Wins:Security:BlockedNames.help: Names that cannot be registered dynamically and are never forwarded to partners or DNS (every suffix), separated by commas.
- WPAD, ISATAP: the defaults. Attack tools use these names to make other machines send traffic to them
A static mapping of one of these names is still answered as usual.
setting.Wins:Security:AllowMultihomedMer: Accept a second address for one name
When a unique name is requested from a second IP and the current owner answers the challenge saying that IP is its own too
(the same machine with two adapters, for example LAN + Wi-Fi):
- ON: keep both IPs under the one name (Multihomed)
- OFF: always refuse the second IP
setting.Wins:Security:MaxDynamicNames.he: How many names clients can register in total.
Stops a flood of random names from exhausting memory.
- At the limit, new names are refused; existing names can still be refreshed
setting.Wins:Security:MaxNamesPerAddress: How many names one IP can register.
- An ordinary Windows machine uses 3 to 6 names
setting.Wins:Security:RateLimitPerSecond: How many packets per second one source IP may keep sending.
Anything above it is dropped unanswered (counted under "Rate limited" on the Overview page).
- An ordinary client sends only a few packets a minute
Raise it if another WINS server or a proxy sends queries for many machines from one IP.
setting.Wins:Security:RateLimitBurst.hel: How many packets one IP may send in one go before the per-second limit applies
(for example a machine that starts and registers several names at once).
Must not be smaller than Requests per second per address.
setting.Wins:Security:MaxConcurrentChall: How many owner checks (challenges) can run at the same time.
Beyond it, a conflicting registration is refused at once.
Stops anyone from using this server to fire queries at many other machines.
setting.Wins:Dns:Enabled.label: Use DNS for unknown names
setting.Wins:Dns:Enabled.help: - ON: when a name is not in the database, replicas or partners, ask DNS as the last resort
Only suffixes 00 / 20 and names that are valid host names are asked.
setting.Wins:Dns:Servers.label: DNS servers
setting.Wins:Dns:Servers.help: IPs of the DNS servers asked directly (UDP 53), separated by commas.
- Empty: the DNS servers this machine's operating system uses
setting.Wins:Dns:Suffix.label: DNS suffix
setting.Wins:Dns:Suffix.help: The domain appended to a name before DNS is asked.
Example: SERVER01 with the suffix corp.local is asked as server01.corp.local
- Empty: ask with the short name as it is
setting.Wins:Dns:TimeoutMs.label: DNS timeout
setting.Wins:Dns:TimeoutMs.help: How long to wait for DNS to answer one name.
The client that asked waits meanwhile, so keep it short.
setting.Wins:Dns:CacheSeconds.label: Remember found names for
setting.Wins:Dns:CacheSeconds.help: How long a "found" answer from DNS is remembered before DNS is asked again.
- 0: never remember, ask DNS every time
setting.Wins:Dns:NegativeCacheSeconds.he: How long a "not found" answer from DNS is remembered,
so that a name that does not exist is not asked of DNS every time.
setting.Wins:ReplicationPort.label: Replication TCP port
setting.Wins:ReplicationPort.help: The port other WinsAlt servers connect to when they copy names from this one.
- Must be allowed in the firewall (Firewall table further down this page)
- Must match the port the other servers have stored for this one
setting.Dashboard:RemoteAccess.label: Open the dashboard to other computers
setting.Dashboard:RemoteAccess.help: - ON: other computers on the network open it at http://<server IP>:<port> (the default for new installations)
- OFF: the dashboard opens only on the server itself (127.0.0.1)
A change needs Save, then Restart service.
If other computers still cannot reach it, press Allow on the dashboard row of the Firewall table further down this page
(the installer has done it already if its firewall option was ticked).
The dashboard is plain HTTP, not encrypted. Change the default password admin / admin right after installing.
setting.Dashboard:RequireSignInToView.he: - ON: nothing is shown before signing in (the default for new installations)
- OFF: anyone who opens the dashboard can look (changing anything always needs a sign-in)
Applies to every computer, the server itself included
(behind a reverse proxy on the same machine, everybody looks like the server).
setting.Dashboard:AllowedHosts.label: Extra host names
setting.Dashboard:AllowedHosts.help: Additional names the dashboard may be opened with, separated by commas.
- IP addresses, localhost and the machine name always work and need not be listed
- A full name such as wins.corp.local must be listed here
This protects against DNS rebinding: a name not on the list is refused.
setting.Dashboard:AdminToken.label: API token for scripts
setting.Dashboard:AdminToken.help: A secret for scripts that call the API without signing in (sent in the X-Admin-Token header).
Whoever holds it can change everything, like an administrator.
- The saved value is never shown again
- Remove the token with the Remove button
Sign in to view this server.
